Hi Soojin,

We started seeing massive tail latency on the streaming chat endpoint this morning during our 08:45–09:15 ingress ramp. p95 is up ~700ms, p99s spiking to 3–3.5s and we've had intermittent 502/connection-dropped errors for SSE clients. Customers are reporting slow typing indicators and message echoing. I attached a short log snippet showing repeated 502s and SSE disconnects tied to connection upgrades.

This is impacting three key customers on our pilot and one live tenant (tier: enterprise). Can Redwood confirm cause and an ETA? We need an update within 30 minutes; our legal and ops teams are asking for immediate mitigation steps.

On Tue, Aug 3, 2027 at 9:22 AM Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — Jia just flagged a P1 affecting Chatterly (hosted us-west). p99s ~3s, 502s, SSE disconnects. Customer asks for a 30m update.

Quick triage results (summary):
- We see a sharp increase in concurrent long-lived SSE connections from several large tenants at 08:40 PDT.
- Front-end proxy (nginx-based) is hitting keepalive connection limits on a subset of pods; connections are queuing at the LB layer which pushes up accept latency. This disproportionately affects upgrades/handshake path and causes short-lived 502s when the proxy drops queued connections.
- Backend inference nodes are healthy; token-generation latency is normal. The tail is introduced earlier (connection/upgrade path).

Immediate mitigations I recommend (fast, low-risk):
1) Increase nginx keepalive and worker_connections for the affected frontend ASG and roll a configuration change to the subset (hotfix). See attached patch.
2) Temporarily route Chatterly traffic to a warmed dedicated SSE proxy pool (we have capacity in us-west-dedicated-2). This avoids the bursting pods and reduces queuing.
3) Reduce proxy-level timeouts for queued connections to fail fast and let clients retry (tradeoff: more retries but lower tail).

I'll push a hotfix (hotfix-proxy-connections.patch) to the canary nodes in 15m and monitor. If the patch doesn't bring p99 under 1s, we should do a traffic redirect.

Logs: /var/log/proxy/sse-upgrades/2027-08-03.gz (summarized in attachment).

-Marcus
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: hotfix-proxy-connections.patch (text/x-patch)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Realtime chat — p99 spike during peak (urgent)

Hi Jia — thanks for the quick flag and logs. We're treating this as P1.

Short-term options you can apply immediately (no code change):
- If acceptable, switch your clients to the non-streaming polling endpoint (POST /v1/chat/poll) for the next 30–60 minutes. Polling will add some overhead but avoids SSE handshake issues.
- Reduce client heartbeat/keepalive to 20s instead of 10s so connections are refreshed less aggressively during retries.

Our operations plan: Marcus will roll a frontend keepalive config hotfix to a canary subset at 10:20 PDT. If that brings p99 under 1s, we'll expand. If not, we'll route you to a dedicated warmed pool at ~10:45 PDT.

We will also offer a one-time service credit for the window impacted; I'll follow up with a formal note and credit proposal.

Proposed emergency call: 10:30 PDT — can you join? If not, we can proceed and update you every 15 minutes.

Grace O'Connor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
